title: Password reset refreshes unsigned attacker-controlled JWTs
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the supplied token with signature verification disabled and only checks that its subject belongs to a user. An attacker can submit an unsigned token naming any existing user and receive a valid signed session token for that account.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with an alg:none token whose payload is {"sub":1} returned 200 and a signed token; that token was accepted by GET /account. The vulnerable decode is at shopapi/auth.py:101-107.

title: JWT signing secret is hardcoded in source
description: SECRET_KEY has a fixed source-controlled value. Anyone who obtains the repository can mint valid HS256 tokens for any existing user, bypassing password authentication and impersonating accounts.
evidence: config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY to "hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d" and auth.py:27 signs all bearer tokens with it; auth.py:42 trusts the same key for every request.

title: Unsigned basket cookie enables arbitrary pickle deserialization
description: The basket cookie is entirely controlled by the client and is deserialized with pickle without a signature or integrity check. A crafted cookie can execute arbitrary Python code in the web process when any basket endpoint reads it.
evidence: shopapi/basket.py:20 calls pickle.loads on request.cookies['basket']; shopapi/basket.py:27 creates the cookie without signing it. A base64-encoded pickle containing an os.system reducer was accepted by GET /basket (HTTP 200), demonstrating the attacker-controlled deserialization path.

title: Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection
description: The search term is concatenated directly into the SQL statement. An unauthenticated caller can alter the WHERE clause and potentially extract or modify database data depending on the database engine and query context.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27+OR+1%3D1+-- returned all six products. The query is built by concatenating q at shopapi/products.py:40-42.

title: Stored review XSS
description: Authenticated users can submit review bodies that are later inserted into the product page with the Jinja safe filter. A reviewer can therefore execute JavaScript in every visitor’s browser.
evidence: POST /products/1/reviews as a normal customer with body '<script>alert(document.domain)</script>' succeeded; GET /p/MUG-SPECK then returned that script verbatim inside the review-body div. Input is stored at shopapi/products.py:90 and rendered with |safe at shopapi/templates/product.html:13.

title: Order detail endpoint lacks ownership authorization
description: The order detail route calls get_order directly instead of own_order, so any authenticated customer who guesses an order ID can read another customer’s order, items, payment totals, refunds, and delivery information.
evidence: Authenticated Priya Shah requested GET /orders/3 and received Tom Okafor’s delivered order, including its BLANKET-WOOL item and payment totals. shopapi/orders.py:46-49 returns get_order(order_id) without checking customer_id.

title: Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses staff check
description: The global admin guard compares request.path to the set of exact route rules. The refund route disables strict slashes, so /admin/refunds/ reaches the handler while not matching the guard’s /admin/refunds path.
evidence: A customer bearer token POSTed to /admin/refunds/ with an order and amount and received 200 with a refund recorded. The bypass is in shopapi/__init__.py:26-41; the slash-tolerant privileged handler is shopapi/admin.py:52-67.

title: Payment status timeout fails open as paid
description: If the payment provider times out, the exception handler sets status to paid and the order is moved to processing with paid_pence equal to the order total. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore allows fulfilment without confirmed payment.
evidence: shopapi/payments.py:37-44 catches requests.Timeout, assigns status = 'paid', and updates the order to processing and fully paid. The comment explicitly describes the timeout as an expected provider condition.

title: Payment webhook trusts attacker-controlled payment amount
description: After checking only a signature derived from the order ID, the webhook marks an awaiting order as processing and copies event.amount_pence into paid_pence without checking it against the order total or provider-side payment record. A validly accepted underpayment can therefore release the order.
evidence: shopapi/payments.py:63 authenticates only webhook_signature(order_id), while lines 69-71 accept any paid event amount and write it directly to paid_pence. No comparison with orders.total_pence or a provider lookup is performed.

title: Stored display name reaches an admin SQL query unsafely
description: A customer controls display_name and can store SQL syntax in it. The staff review-report query interpolates that stored value into SQL, enabling a second-order SQL injection when staff view the report.
evidence: A customer was able to set display_name to x' OR 1=1 -- via PATCH /account; the subsequent staff GET /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=1 returned reviews matching the injected predicate. The vulnerable f-string is shopapi/admin.py:77-82.

title: Passwords use fast unsalted SHA-256
description: Password hashes are generated with bare SHA-256 and no per-user salt or work factor. A database disclosure permits efficient offline cracking and makes identical passwords trivially identifiable.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:15-20 hashes passwords as hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() and compares the result directly. The same scheme is used to seed all demo accounts in scripts/seed.py:32-33.

title: Approved-host image fetch follows redirects without revalidation
description: The URL allowlist and public-IP check apply only to the initial hostname. requests.get follows redirects by default, so an approved CDN or supplier URL that redirects to an internal address can make the server fetch internal resources.
evidence: shopapi/images.py:28-35 validates only u.hostname, while shopapi/images.py:50 calls requests.get(url, ...) with the default redirect behavior and no validation of each redirect destination.

title: Application entry point enables Flask debug mode
description: Running the documented application entry point starts Flask with debug=True. In a deployed or accidentally exposed instance this can disclose stack traces and enable the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which can lead to code execution.
evidence: run.py:5-6 calls app.run(host='127.0.0.1', port=5000, debug=True); there is no environment-gated production check.
